summaries.demographer: Clairemarie Merchant is a 54-year-old White, non-Hispanic, U.S.-born woman living in Newton, Illinois, with her husband Mark (Q84-Q89, Q51). She has a high school diploma plus trade credentials and works as a construction laborer, placing her in a skilled working-class household with moderate but cautious financial stability (Q90, Q65, Q83). She is married, has two adult children, and remains embedded in a local kin network including her mother and sister (Q05-Q07). Her life course reflects long-term residence in rural/small-town Illinois and strong church/community attachment (Q01, Q47, Q97).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Clairemarie is highly planful, budget-conscious, and loss-averse, using named savings buckets, pantry stocking, written schedules, and fixed travel allowances to manage uncertainty (Q15, Q61-Q62). Her choices reveal strong present responsibility but also forward-looking investment in credentials, retirement stability, and possible subcontracting work (Q18, Q83, Q108). She responds to risk through checklists and prevention, whether in finances, jobsite safety, or health care (Q03, Q40, Q65). Peer and community influence matters, but she filters it through practical competence rather than status or trend-seeking (Q24, Q48).
summaries.political_scientist: Clairemarie is a frequent voter who emphasizes local races, public safety, infrastructure, schools, and taxes (Q23). She identifies as a moderate Republican or Republican-leaning independent, with issue-by-issue flexibility around food support, health access, and worker training (Q24, Q95-Q96). Her civic orientation is communitarian and institutionally pragmatic: she values churches, food banks, competent local government, and accountable law enforcement (Q17, Q20, Q47). On race and policing, she reports being affected somewhat by Black Lives Matter and supports accountability without rejecting police as an institution (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Clairemarie presents as conscientious, orderly, duty-driven, and practically nurturing, with a strong identity built around competence, reliability, and service (Q01, Q15, Q109). She copes with stress through lists, prayer, movement, quilting, and selective social support from Mark, Denise, Linda, and church friends (Q43-Q45). Her anxiety appears tied to uncertainty, safety risks, and schedule disruption rather than generalized helplessness (Q45, Q78). She is future-oriented but grounded, seeking advancement that preserves identity while adapting to age-related physical limits (Q31, Q50, Q108).
